source: Constructed document — based on standard Grade 8 geometry curriculum
notes: Constructed document designed to cover complex rhetorical patterns absent in CK-12 lessons: ECU nesting depth 3, orbit-2 satellites, a unit serving as nucleus in one relation and satellite in another. Covers AA similarity, SSS similarity, SAS similarity, scale factor, and real-world application (shadow method). Class B-C boundary: 20 units, 7 ECUs.

units.label: Title: Similar Triangles and Proportional Reasoning
units.content_summary: Lesson title

units.label: Hook: estimating tree height using shadows (image)
units.content_summary: Photograph of a person standing next to a tree. Both cast shadows. Labels: person height = 1.8m, person shadow = 2.4m, tree shadow = 10m. Question: 'How can you find the tree's height without climbing it?'

units.label: Hook explanation: shadow method (text)
units.content_summary: Explains that the person and tree form similar triangles with the sun's rays. Since the triangles are similar, corresponding sides are proportional: person_height/person_shadow = tree_height/tree_shadow → 1.8/2.4 = h/10 → h=7.5m. Establishes the need for similarity theory.

units.label: Learning Objectives (text)
units.content_summary: Objectives: define similar triangles; apply AA, SSS, SAS similarity criteria; calculate scale factor and unknown sides; solve real-world problems using similar triangles.

units.label: Definition: similar triangles (text)
units.content_summary: Two triangles are similar (~) if: (1) all corresponding angles are equal AND (2) all corresponding sides are proportional. Similar ≠ congruent: similar triangles have the same shape but not necessarily the same size. Symbol: △ABC ~ △DEF.

units.label: Similar vs congruent diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Three pairs of triangles: (1) congruent pair (same shape, same size); (2) similar pair (same shape, different sizes); (3) neither (different shape and size). Labels: ≅ for congruent, ~ for similar, ≁ for neither.

units.label: Scale factor definition (text)
units.content_summary: Scale factor k = (side in larger triangle)/(corresponding side in smaller triangle). If △ABC ~ △DEF with scale factor k=2, then every side of △DEF is 2× the corresponding side of △ABC. Angles are unchanged by scaling.

units.label: AA Similarity Criterion (text)
units.content_summary: Angle-Angle (AA): if two angles of one triangle equal two angles of another, the triangles are similar. Sufficient because triangle angles sum to 180° — if two match, the third must also match. Most commonly used criterion. Does not require knowing any side lengths.

units.label: AA Similarity proof diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Diagram showing two triangles △ABC and △DEF with angles A=D=50° and B=E=70° marked. Third angles C=F=60° derived. Arrows show the correspondence. Sides proportional by ratio DE/AB = EF/BC = DF/AC.

units.label: AA Similarity worked example (text)
units.content_summary: Problem: △PQR has angles 40°, 60°, 80°. △XYZ has angles 40° and 60°. Are they similar? Yes, by AA (two angles match, third is automatically 80°). Find XZ if PQ=6, PR=9, XY=4. Solution: scale factor k=4/6=2/3, XZ=PR×k=9×(2/3)=6.

units.label: SSS Similarity Criterion (text)
units.content_summary: Side-Side-Side (SSS): if all three pairs of corresponding sides are proportional, the triangles are similar. Must check: AB/DE = BC/EF = AC/DF = k (same ratio for all three pairs). Unlike SSS congruence, sides need not be equal — only proportional.

units.label: SAS Similarity Criterion (text)
units.content_summary: Side-Angle-Side (SAS): if two pairs of corresponding sides are proportional AND the included angles are equal, the triangles are similar. The angle must be between the two proportional sides. Important: proportional sides + non-included angle is NOT sufficient for similarity.

units.label: Criteria comparison table (image)
units.content_summary: Three-column table: Criterion | What to Check | Example. Rows: AA (2 angles equal, easy to apply), SSS (all 3 side ratios equal, need all sides), SAS (2 side ratios equal + included angle equal, need 2 sides + angle between them).

units.label: Proportional sides calculation method (text)
units.content_summary: Setting up proportions: identify corresponding vertices (matching angle order). Write proportion: a/d = b/e = c/f. Cross-multiply to solve for unknown. Check: all ratios should equal the scale factor k. Common error: misidentifying corresponding sides.

units.label: Proportional calculation warning (image)
units.content_summary: Side-by-side: CORRECT proportion setup with matching vertices highlighted in same colour vs INCORRECT setup with mismatched vertices. Red X on wrong setup, green check on correct. Caption: 'Always match angles first, then sides.'

units.label: Real-world application: shadow method full solution (text)
units.content_summary: Returns to opening problem. Full formal solution: △(person, tip of shadow, base of person) ~ △(tree, tip of shadow, base of tree) by AA (both have right angle at base + same sun angle). Scale factor = 10/2.4. Tree height = 1.8 × (10/2.4) = 7.5m. Includes diagram.

units.label: Shadow method solution diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Diagram showing person-shadow triangle and tree-shadow triangle as two similar right triangles sharing the sun-angle vertex at the tip of the shadows. Corresponding sides and angles labeled. Solution steps annotated.

units.label: Extension: indirect measurement techniques (text)
units.content_summary: Other indirect measurement methods using similar triangles: (1) mirror method — place mirror between object and observer, use angle of reflection; (2) transit/theodolite — measure angle from two known points; (3) GPS/satellite triangulation. All rely on similar triangle proportionality.

units.label: Practice problems set (text)
units.content_summary: Six problems: identify similarity criterion; find unknown sides; determine scale factor; set up and solve shadow-method problem; identify which pairs of triangles are similar from given information; multi-step problem combining AA and proportional reasoning.
